reference.title: Dumbbell Standing Overhead Press
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Shoulders, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in at the shoulders and brace, breathe out as you press; breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; the EMG studies used 80% of 1RM (Saeterbakken 2013; Saeterbakken 2012)
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; single-arm or alternating standing press

cues.text: Stand tall, feet about hip width, knees soft, ribs down and glutes lightly braced. Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward, elbows under the wrists and a little in front.
Breathe out and press up and slightly in; keep the ribs down and glutes tight.
Arms nearly straight overhead, dumbbells over the shoulders, head through.
Lower in about 2 s to shoulder height, elbows under the wrists.
Brace again at the shoulders and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back and arching the low back
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and brace the abs; lighter dumbbells.

mistakes.mistake: Using the legs to bounce the weight up
mistakes.fix: Knees stay soft and still (a push press is a different exercise).

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring straight out or behind the body
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows a little in front (scapular plane).
Lower to about shoulder height and press to nearly straight arms.

kinematics.norm: From about 80-90 degrees at the bottom to about 160-170 degrees overhead (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the bottom with the forearms vertical, nearly straight at the top (clinical opinion)
Elbows about 20-40 degrees in front of the frontal plane (scapular plane; clinical opinion)
Upright and stacked, knees soft; standing presses demand much more trunk activity than seated (Saeterbakken 2012)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #042612, Dumbbell Standing Overhead Press, video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Bring the dumbbells to the shoulders with a controlled curl or clean, and lower them the same way.
modify: Shoulder pain overhead: press with palms facing in and elbows further forward.
Low-back discomfort: press seated with back support or half-kneeling.
progressions: Z press (no leg or back support).

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover. The shoulder press gave the highest anterior deltoid activity of four exercises (Campos 2020); standing and dumbbells gave more deltoid activity than seated and barbell (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main mover. The shoulder press gave the highest anterior deltoid activity of four exercises (Campos 2020); standing and dumbbells gave more deltoid activity than seated and barbell (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lifts the arms up and out; medial deltoid activity in the press was close to the lateral raise (Campos 2020) and higher standing than seated (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Lifts the arms up and out; medial deltoid activity in the press was close to the lateral raise (Campos 2020) and higher standing than seated (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows in the top half.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows in the top half.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blades overhead.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blades overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades so the arms reach fully overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades so the arms reach fully overhead.
muscleNotes.pec_r: The clavicular head helps at the bottom, with the elbows forward.
muscleNotes.pec_l: The clavicular head helps at the bottom, with the elbows forward.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder; higher standing than seated (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder; higher standing than seated (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the ball of the shoulder.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the ball of the shoulder.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down and the trunk stacked; rectus abdominis activity was about 81% lower seated than standing in the bilateral dumbbell press (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the spine tall under the load.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the spine tall under the load.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Squeezed to keep the pelvis level and stop the low back arching.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Squeezed to keep the pelvis level and stop the low back arching.
